transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-30
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CTO, HarvestAI), Omar Khalid (Lead ML Eng), Lisa Nguyen (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, short):
HarvestAI is exploring Redwood for streaming and burst-heavy workloads. Primary concerns: p95 latency targets for user-facing streams, steady-state throughput / tokens-per-second, and private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS). They've seen inconsistent p95s on their current Triton-based cluster during bursts. Next: Redwood to run a 7-day benchmark using HarvestAI prompts; share pricing and security docs.

Topics:
- Current infra + pain points
- p95 targets, concurrency, and streaming expectations
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Benchmark plan + data/sample prompts
- Security / compliance questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, Maya from Redwood here, thanks for taking the time. Can you quickly run through who you have on the call?
[00:06] Priya Singh: Yeah hi, Priya here, CTO at HarvestAI. Omar's our lead on model infra, and Lisa from SRE is gonna be the network/compliance touchpoint.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Awesome. Lucas is our solutions engineer, he'll lead on the latency/profiling stuff.
[00:18] Lucas Park: Hey all. Quick agenda, wanna understand your p95 goals, current throughput, and see if Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. Then propose a benchmark run. Sound good?
[00:26] Priya Singh: Perfect. Our product is real-time summarization for agritech field inspectors. Typical user flow is a short 1-3k token prompt, but we also have longer 8k note aggregation behind the scenes. Need streamable response for the inspector UI, so p95 is critical.
[00:40] Omar Khalid: To add: peak times are after harvest windows, roughly 2 hours/day where RPS jumps x6, we see sustained concurrency up to 220 simultaneous streams and spiky bursts to ~850 requests in a minute.
[00:55] Lisa Nguyen: From SRE, we need audit logs, KMS integration, and strict VPC controls — can't have sample data leave our VPC unless explicitly allowed.
[01:05] Lucas Park: Got it. Quick question on p95: what number are you targeting for the UI? Are we talking 200ms, 500ms, 1s?
[01:12] Priya Singh: Ideally p95 sub-300ms for the streaming token arrival for short prompts. For the long 8k jobs, p95 under 1.2s is acceptable because those are background. But the UI must feel instant.
[01:25] Maya Patel: That's helpful. For streaming, sub-300ms p95 is ambitious but achievable depending on model and deployment mode. Hosted can hit lower latencies because of our optimized runtime and global edge routing; Dedicated gives you predictable tail latency at scale; Private is possible but depends on on-prem hardware and our private control plane latency to your VPC.
[01:46] Omar Khalid: Right now our Triton cluster gives us p95s around 650-900ms under burst and token churn is high due to multi-turn context. We're evaluating quantized LLaMA variants and a custom KV cache, but we keep seeing overhead on the request path.
[02:03] Lucas Park: Sounds familiar. Two quick levers: batching vs continuous prefix/KV caching and model variant selection (8-bit quant vs 4-bit). Also kernel selection — our runtime picks optimized CUDA kernels per sequence length to avoid token-time spikes.
[02:18] Priya Singh: Curious about multiplexing — do you have any multiplexing or request coalescing features so small prompts don't wait behind big ones?
[02:26] Lucas Park: Yes, we support workload-aware multiplexing and request shapers. We can prioritize UI low-latency streams and put large background jobs on slower queues or Dedicated pools.
[02:34] Lisa Nguyen: From SRE: how are you measuring p95? Our current tooling uses Prometheus histograms and an internal token-emission metric. We need metrics we can align on.
[02:44] Maya Patel: We'll align on tail-latency at the token emission level — we typically report p50/p95/p99 for token latency and end-to-end request latencies. For benchmarking we'll provide a harness that emits token-level timings and a CSV so you can import to your dashboards.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Ok. Can you ballpark token/sec throughput? For background jobs we need to handle up to ~5M tokens/day, and during the 2-hour peak that roughly maps to 2.5k tokens/sec sustained, with bursts hitting 12k tokens/sec for a couple minutes.
[03:18] Lucas Park: Preliminary numbers: on a Dedicated 8xA100 pool with KV cache we see stable 6k-10k tokens/sec for medium-sized models (7B-13B) with p95 in the 150-350ms range for streaming short prompts. Hosted pinning to a high-perf region and edge routing can lower p95 but dedicated predictability matters when you have that 850-rps spike.
[03:41] Omar Khalid: Do you have examples where you've hit 10k+ tokens/sec in-hosted? We worry about noisy neighbors on hosted tiers.
[03:49] Maya Patel: For higher-tier hosted customers we run isolated tenant slices and capacity reservations. But for predictable spikes like yours, Dedicated or a hybrid model with autoscaled Dedicated + burst to Hosted is a common pattern.
[04:03] Priya Singh: Hybrid seems interesting — primary on Dedicated, fall back to Hosted during extreme spikes?
[04:08] Lucas Park: Exactly. We can set policy-based routing: prefer Dedicated, if queue depth or latency passes threshold, route overflow to Hosted variants with compatible model quant and version.
[04:19] Lisa Nguyen: Security — private deployment: can we run the inference runtime fully in our VPC so no request payload leaves? We want to bring HSM/KMS, audit logging.
[04:28] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane option. We can integrate with your KMS/HSM, keep logs in your S3, and provide RBAC/SAML SSO. Note: operational latency can be slightly higher if you run on smaller GPUs than our hosted fleet — we'll profile that.
[04:46] Omar Khalid: For the benchmark, we want to compare three configs: our Triton baseline, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private on our on-prem GPUs (NVIDIA H100 cluster). We need a fair apples-to-apples test for p95 and tokens/sec.
[04:59] Lucas Park: Makes sense. We'll prepare a benchmark harness that runs your 3 prompt types (short UI, medium 3k, long 8k), with ramp patterns that mirror your 2-hour surge and minute-level bursts. We'll collect token-level latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.
[05:18] Priya Singh: Any gotchas with long sequences? We saw memory spikes and KV eviction thrashing on certain quantized builds.
[05:26] Lucas Park: We recommend sequence-aware kernel selection and chunked attention for long sequences. Also, persistent KV cache with eviction policy tuned by usage helps — we'll include recommendations for cache sizing.
[05:37] Maya Patel: For long jobs, p95 end-to-end will be higher but token emission smoothing can be tuned so early tokens emit faster — improves perceived latency for the user.
[05:47] Lisa Nguyen: Network wise, during burst we might hit egress limits. Does Redwood support co-locating inference and control plane in our VPC to minimize egress?
[05:57] Maya Patel: For Private, yes. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide peering and private endpoints that minimize public bandwidth. We'll document expected egress and bandwidth for your peak patterns.
[06:08] Omar Khalid: About model variants — we may want to try 13B quantized and a trimmed 3B for UI. Can you serve heterogeneous model sizes and route by latency requirements?
[06:18] Lucas Park: Yes. Route by policy: short prompts -> fast 3B low-latency model; longer context -> 13B with KV cache. We also surface model cost per-token to help tradeoffs.
[06:29] Priya Singh: Pricing — we need committed monthly pricing for Dedicated similar to reserved capacity. Also, for a POC can we get a short trial window?
[06:38] Maya Patel: We typically do a 7-14 day benchmark POC; for Dedicated we can offer a short reserved window or pilot credits. We'll include pricing tiers.
[06:46] Lucas Park: I'll include recommended pool sizing: for your 220 steady concurrency and 850 burst, a preliminary suggestion is 4-6 x A100 equivalent nodes with autoscale headroom to double for bursts, plus a small Hosted spillover. We'll refine after the initial benchmark.
[06:59] Lisa Nguyen: Can we get the audit evidence for SOC2 and the SLA? We're collecting everything for procurement.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Yes — action item, we'll share security packet and explicit SLA terms.
[07:11] Priya Singh: Great. Anything else on instrumentation? We want traces tied to tokens, not just request ids.
[07:18] Lucas Park: We can emit tracing hooks and sample spans per token, plus per-request KV cache metrics. We'll share the exporters (Prometheus / OTLP) config.
[07:28] Priya Singh: Timeline: assuming benchmark looks good, we want to be in pilot by end of Q4 and production early Q1. Is that realistic?
[07:36] Maya Patel: That's reasonable. We'll aim to have the benchmark plan executed in early September and iterate.
[07:42] Omar Khalid: Quick note — competitors we talked to were pushing managed inference but with higher latencies. If Redwood's Dedicated can actually hit sub-300ms p95 for UI streams, that's a differentiator.
[07:54] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll focus the benchmark on token-p95 for the UI path.
[07:59] Priya Singh: Ok last thing — can you include an example of the fallback policy for when Dedicated is saturated? We want to see fail-open vs queue behaviors.
[08:07] Lucas Park: We'll include a policy doc: overflow to Hosted model variant, queue depth thresholds, and canary routing to gradually shift traffic.
[08:15] Maya Patel: Perfect. Recap of next steps...
[08:18] Maya Patel (recap): Redwood to share: 1) Dedicated vs Hosted pricing matrix + SLA, 2) SOC2/ISO packet and Private deployment guide, 3) benchmark plan + harness, 4) sample routing/fallback policy. HarvestAI to share: 1) representative prompts and traffic patterns, 2) on-prem H100 cluster details, 3) compliance contacts.
[08:36] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Omar Khalid: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:40] Lisa Nguyen: Thanks.
